items.body:
## Motivation

A request with `return_sampling_mask` or a `sampling_logprobs_mode` makes the sampler capture each sampled token's filtered distribution. Its kept mass was `torch.where(weights > 0, weights, 0).sum(...)`, but every capture path hands over post-filter probabilities that are already zero outside the support, so the `where` builds a full-vocabulary copy of the weights before summing them. It is a measurable part of the capture's per-step cost at larger batches.

## Modifications

- The kept mass is `weights.sum(dim=-1, dtype=torch.float32)`.

items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Preserve vLLM's `finish_reason="length"` in `TokenOutput.stop_reason`. Today the vLLM rollout server reports `completed` both when generation stops naturally and when the output budget cuts it off. A caller translating this value to the Anthropic Messages API consequently sends `end_turn` for a truncated response, and the client can exit with work still in progress.

### Design and compatibility

Map vLLM's `stop` to `completed` and let `length` pass through the existing fallback. Callers can now return `max_tokens` to Anthropic clients. Abort still maps to `aborted`

## Purpose

Related: #66070

HF's Qwen3.5 / Qwen3-VL vision tower computes RoPE frequencies, cos/sin and the Q/K rotation in FP32, then casts back. `Qwen3_VisionTransformer` builds its rotary cache with `get_rope(...)` without a dtype, so the cache takes the model's default dtype (BF16) and the angles are rounded before the rotation.

MiniMax-H3-Image runs a fixed six-step PDD schedule, so its AdaLN outputs are a release invariant: every process start rebuilds the same plans by streaming the 24.2 GiB `adaln_proj` weights. `--minimax-h3-adaln-cache-path` already exists for the video variants (prebuilt sidecar, `format_version=2`), but the image pipeline rejected it outright with `ValueError("MiniMax H3 image does not support an AdaLN cache")`.

This PR lets an image release load a prebuilt sidecar, so single-shot and serving deployments skip the rebuild and do not keep `adaln_proj` resident.

items.summary: Fixes incorrect end-to-start marker pairing in build_image_bounds, preventing negative canvas spans and degraded visual-question-answering accuracy in MiniCPM-V 4.7.
items.body:
## Purpose
Fixes #67360.

`build_image_bounds()` in `minicpmv4_7.py` paired span markers by index. A `</image>` (or `<image>`, `<slice>`, `</slice>`) written in message text is tokenized to the same special id as the processor's marker. When such a marker comes before an image, every later pair is shifted and `_assign_canvas_span` gets a negative span. Canvas M-RoPE then falls back to sequential positions for all images in the request. The client sees no error, but accuracy drops: on ChartQA (500 items, greedy) it went from 87.8% to 78.8%. Details are in the issue.

This PR pairs each end mark

Multi-turn agentic workloads often combine long, growing conversation histories with relatively short outputs. In Prefill/Decode (P/D) disaggregated serving, these workloads can concentrate pressure on Prefiller instances, especially during request bursts.

The Decoder that served the previous turn may still hold a substantial reusable prefix in its local KV cache, including tokens generated during that turn. items.summary: A host KV pool can be backed by host memory allocated with the CUDA VMM API ( with a location, e.g. Grace DRAM), mapped for both the GPU and the CPU at one virtual address.

## Motivation

A host KV pool can be backed by host memory allocated with the CUDA VMM API (`cuMemCreate` with a `CU_MEM_LOCATION_TYPE_HOST_NUMA` location, e.g. Grace DRAM), mapped for both the GPU and the CPU at one virtual address. For an interior pointer into such an allocation, `cudaHostGetDevicePointer` returns `cudaSuccess` but resolves to the start of the allocation. The JIT `runtime::get_device_accessible_ptr` (`sgl_kernel/runtime.cuh`) passes CPU tensors through it, so a JIT kernel handed a per-layer slice of such a pool silently reads layer 0's bytes.

items.author: amd-preetesh
items.summary: MTP verification did not reach it: on current the TurboQuant metadata builder opts out of spec-as-decode, so a k-token verify is classified as a prefill and never enters the UltraQuant decode kernel. Keep an MTP verify on the UltraQuant decode path.
items.body:
## Purpose

UltraQuant decode already ships. MTP verification did not reach it: on current `main` the TurboQuant metadata builder opts out of spec-as-decode, so a k-token verify is classified as a prefill and never enters the UltraQuant decode kernel.

items.author: Shr3yash
items.summary: Batch acquire looks up adapter ids under the registry lock, then bumps the usage counters after dropping it. A queued unload can run in that gap, see zero users, and drop the adapter.
items.body:
## Motivation

Batch acquire looks up adapter ids under the registry lock, then bumps the usage counters after dropping it. A queued unload can run in that gap, see zero users, and drop the adapter. The request keeps going, and release() raises KeyError.

Same hole as the draft in #42971, which was closed unmerged.

## Modifications

Do the lookup and the counter bump together under the writer lock. If acquire is cancelled after a partial bump, roll those back even if we're cancelled again. release() no-ops when the counter is already gone.

items.author: metamergebot
items.summary: Adds an AbortHook trait that notifies packages of which specific request IDs were aborted, enabling distinction between client cancellations and server-initiated aborts.
items.body:
Stacked on #50189; only the top commit (25 files, all under `rust/sglang-server/`) is this change.

## Motivation

A package that serves through `Server::start_with_extensions` and keeps its own per-request records has no way to learn which requests a client aborted. An abort by rid reaches the frontend through three entries: the listener's `/abort_request`, the gRPC `Abort`, and, under attention DP, the abort another DP rank's listener relays to `/internal/peer`. A package's HTTP layer sees only the first of them, so it cannot tell a request the client cancelled from one the server ended.

items.title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Pass attention metadata to the connector on piecewise steps
items.author: MatthewBonanni
items.summary: Fixes HiSparse KV connector crashing under mixed (piecewise/eager) CUDA graph steps by passing attn_metadata consistently, preventing unbounded swap-row counter growth.
items.body:
## Overview

MRv2 passes `attn_metadata` to the KV connector's `pre_forward` only on FULL CUDA graph steps. On piecewise and eager steps the HiSparse connector gets `None`, so `prepare_forward` skips its per-forward setup. That setup resets the swap-row step counter and binds the batch's decode/prefill state.

DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM hide this because their attention layers call `prepare_for_batch` themselves. Kimi-K3.1's fused DSA path doesn't, so the step counter keeps growing across mixed steps until the worker raises:

```
ValueError: HiSparse swap rows exceed the configured speculative deco

items.title: [Bugfix][Security] Check the uncompressed size of embedding archives before torch.load
items.author: LeizhenZhang
items.summary: Checks embedding archive uncompressed sizes before torch.load to prevent zip-bomb DoS attacks, reducing peak memory from 3 GiB to ~1 MiB for compressed zero payloads.
items.body:
## Overview

`VLLM_MAX_EMBED_DECODE_BYTES` (#54632) bounds the dense size of a client-supplied `prompt_embeds`, `image_embeds`, `audio_embeds` or `video_embeds` tensor. The check runs after `torch.load`. A `torch.save` archive is a zip file, and `torch.load` reads each storage entry at the uncompressed size the archive records, so a deflate-compressed storage of zeros inflates to many GiB inside `torch.load` before the check runs. A one-row view of such a storage passes the check and keeps the whole storage alive. This PR checks the archive's uncompressed size before calling `torch.load`.

items.author: LeizhenZhang

items.title: [Feat] dp-controller: Keep a routing key on one DP rank (--load-balance-method follow_routing_key)
items.author: nanjiangwill
items.summary: With DP attention each DP rank keeps its own prefix cache. SGLang's gateway keeps a session's turns on the rank that holds its history by treating each rank as a worker: with, its and policies route by.
items.body:
## Motivation

With DP attention each DP rank keeps its own prefix cache. SGLang's gateway keeps a session's turns on the rank that holds its history by treating each rank as a worker: with `--dp-aware`, its `manual` and `consistent_hashing` policies route by `X-SMG-Routing-Key`. A front door that sees only the engine, not its ranks (a router that balances engines, or a generic load balancer), keeps a session on one engine, but inside it the DP controller spreads the session's turns over every rank, so most turns miss their own history.

The request already carries the key: `X-SMG-Routing-Key`

items.title: [Fix] embedding: Normalize FP16 pooled embeddings in float32
items.author: Afloat16
items.summary: FP16 pooling can return NaNs for zero embeddings because 's epsilon rounds to zero. A finite embedding whose norm exceeds FP16's range instead normalizes to an all-zero vector, and subnormal embeddings lose normalization accuracy.
items.body:
## Motivation

FP16 pooling can return NaNs for zero embeddings because `F.normalize`'s epsilon rounds to zero. A finite embedding whose norm exceeds FP16's range instead normalizes to an all-zero vector, and subnormal embeddings lose normalization accuracy. These results can propagate to cosine retrieval scores, including after dimension truncation.

## Modifications

Promote FP16 pooled embeddings to float32 before computing the norm and division, then cast the normalized result back to its input dtype. Apply the same helper to the dense and ragged-dimension output paths. BF16, float32, floa

items.title: [Feat] http_server: Compress response bodies for clients that accept zstd
items.author: nanjiangwill
items.summary: Responses that carry routed experts, sampling masks or top logprobs run to megabytes per request. A client in another region, or behind a proxy that bills egress per byte, pays for every one.
items.body:
## Motivation

Responses that carry routed experts, sampling masks or top logprobs run to megabytes per request. A client in another region, or behind a proxy that bills egress per byte, pays for every one. SGLang decompresses zstd request bodies (`SGLANG_ENABLE_REQUEST_DECOMPRESSION`) but never compresses a response.

This adds the standard HTTP negotiation for responses: the client lists `zstd` in `Accept-Encoding` and the server answers with `Content-Encoding: zstd` and `Vary: Accept-Encoding`, which curl, httpx, aiohttp and requests decode on their own when their zstd support is installed.

items.title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Fix HF3FS storage rank derivation with pipeline parallelism
items.author: xsxszab
items.summary: Fixes HF3FSKVConnector rank collision under pipeline parallelism by deriving storage rank from both PP and TP ranks so each stage writes distinct data files.
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

`HF3FSKVConnector` uses the TP rank alone as its storage rank. With pipeline parallelism, workers of different stages that share a TP rank write the same data file (`hf3fs_vllm_data_file_<rank>`) and register as the same metadata rank, although they hold different layers. KV loaded back from HF3FS then contains another stage's layers and the outputs are garbage.

This PR derives the storage rank as `pp_rank * tp_size + tp_rank`, so every (PP, TP) rank has its own data file and metadata rank.

## Claims

- With PP > 1, KV loaded back from HF3FS reprod

items.author: jiejingzhangamd
items.summary: The ROCm top-k v2 split path uses one persistent scratch workspace per device. Its histogram and counters are reset by the split kernels themselves, so concurrent launches on different streams race the same memory and can leave invalid top-k indices.

## Motivation

The ROCm top-k v2 split path uses one persistent scratch workspace per device. Its histogram and counters are reset by the split kernels themselves, so concurrent launches on different streams race the same memory and can leave invalid top-k indices. CUDA/HIP graph capture adds another case: graphs captured on one stream bake the same workspace pointers into their kernel arguments, then may be replayed concurrently on different streams.

## Modifications

- Bind the ROCm split workspace to the first eager stream that uses it. Other eager streams fall back to the existing one-blo

items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Restore bounded layered LoRA collection for FSDP1 layouts with flattened parameters or independently wrapped adapter leaves. The collector currently checks local parameter names, passes local keys to PEFT, and recursively summons nested units. These behaviors can drop adapters or export a nested `_flat_param`. An empty result then triggers a full-model CPU summon on every FSDP1 rank, defeating the memory bound requested by layered collection.

Initialize FSDP1 from its real root, recognize original flat-parameter names and leaf prefixes, normalize parameter ownership

items.author: lzl86
items.summary: Prefer over (FA3) for ordinary causal attention on Hopper when using / KV cache. In #66590 and our local H100 verification, this yields ~12% higher decode throughput and substantially better cross-run repeatability.
items.body:
## Summary

Prefer `FLASHINFER` over `FLASH_ATTN` (FA3) for ordinary causal attention on Hopper (`SM90`) when using `fp8` / `fp8_e4m3` KV cache. Relates to #66590.

- **Why:** On SM90 with FP8 KV cache, the default FA3 path quantizes Q to FP8, whereas FlashInfer's SM90 XQA decode keeps Q in BF16/FP16. In #66590 and our local H100 verification, this yields ~12% higher decode throughput and substantially better cross-run repeatability.
- **Scope & Fallback:** Only affects SM90 ordinary causal attention with `kv_cache_dtype in ("fp8", "fp8_e4m3")`. MLA, non-causal, multimodal prefix, BF16/auto KV

items.author: MatthewBonanni

`SharedOffloadRegion` reserves address space for segmented regions with `os.memfd_create`. Python builds made against old glibc headers do not have that function. AttributeError: module 'os' has no attribute 'memfd_create'
```

items.body:
Add script `tools/tune_flashinfer_bf16_gemm.py` that for given model, tp topoligies list, and batch sizes list generates json file with results of FI gemm BF16 autotuning, so for each gemm BF16 layer of the model we get kernel winner.

Then this json file vLLM searches in ~/.cache/flashinfer and loads the result, so autotuning in inference will be skip which saves 20-30 minutes time on cold-start.

Original author: @kpham-sgl (Khoa Pham); credited with a `Co-authored-by` trailer in the port commit.

Takes only the per-forward int64 `cu_seqlens` reuse from `f87a6998703`. The pinned FlashInfer 0.7.4 casts int32 sequence offsets to a new int64 tensor on each KDA prefill call, while its host-metadata cache keys on the live tensor identity. items.summary: Deterministic mode refuses AITER decode attention for MLA models (DeepSeek-V2/V3/R1, Kimi K2, Moonlight,...), so they decode on Triton MLA, the slowest part of their deterministic step. The reason: AITER picks the MLA decode KV split count from the batch size …
items.body:
## Motivation

Deterministic mode refuses AITER decode attention for MLA models (DeepSeek-V2/V3/R1, Kimi K2, Moonlight, ...), so they decode on Triton MLA, the slowest part of their deterministic step. The reason: AITER picks the MLA decode KV split count from the batch size and the total KV length, and its persistent kernel schedules work across the batch, so a request's output depends on its batchmates.

With a fixed split count, AITER's split-KV MLA decode kernel gives every request the same output at any batch size, at 16 heads per GPU. This PR uses it in deterministic mode.

items.title: fix(sampler): ensure deterministic index ordering in top_k_per_row_prefill
items.author: devtyagi3909
items.summary: fixes #67192 selects top-k elements across histogram passes, with bins strictly below the threshold bin written directly to via slot reservation. because threads win atomic reservations in non-deterministic arrival order, the returned row indices are permuted …
items.body:
fixes #67192

`top_k_per_row_prefill` selects top-k elements across histogram passes, with bins strictly below the threshold bin written directly to `smemOutput` via `atomicAdd` slot reservation. because threads win atomic reservations in non-deterministic arrival order, the returned row indices are permuted across runs with identical inputs. downstream flashinfer sparse attention accumulates in output index order, causing bf16 numerical drift across layers.

this sorts `smemOutput` by index prior to writing out to global memory when `!multipleBlocksPerRow` (prefill and merged decode passes),

good catch on the 2048 scaling. swapped the rank loop for `cub::BlockRadixSort` (aliasing `smemFinal.indexSort` in the existing union so zero extra smem footprint), padding with `INT_MAX` for `idx >= topK` via `SortBlockedToStriped`. pushes

items.title: [Fix] scheduler: Count the unprefilled part of a chunked request in total_tokens load
items.author: cuihangbin
items.summary: With, the DP controller routes each request to the rank with the smallest. That value is described as "KV tokens in use plus queued request tokens", but it misses one request: the one in chunked prefill.
items.body:
## Motivation

With `--load-balance-method total_tokens`, the DP controller routes each request to the rank with the
smallest `num_total_tokens`. That value is described as "KV tokens in use plus queued request tokens",
but it misses one request: the one in chunked prefill. That request holds KV only for the chunks it
has already run, and it is in neither the running batch nor the waiting queue. So a rank that has
just started a 64K-token prompt reports only about one chunk of load, and new requests keep going to
it.

We saw this on 2×H20 with Qwen3.8-27B-FP8, TP=2, `--attn-dp-size 2`

items.body:
`nightly-test-ppu.yml` carried its own `0 16 * * *` schedule. It started at the same moment as `release-docker-ppu-nightly.yml`, knew nothing about whether the build succeeded, and tested a hardcoded base image plus a fresh `pip install -e` of whatever commit it happened to check out.

So the image the nightly builds was never the thing under test. A broken image could pass every case; a good image could fail because the source install had drifted from it. Two independent crons racing on the same clock also meant "which image was actually tested" had no answer after the fact.

The Transformers modeling backend materializes meta parameters in the model dtype, discarding the dtype the modeling declared. A modeling that stores weights as fp8 with fp32 scales therefore gets them in bf16: the weights take twice the memory and the scales are rounded. This PR keeps the declared dtype, as `from_pretrained` does.

## Details

vLLM builds the Transformers model with `from_config` ([here](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/94febce7563ae2d67a062dc0f8ab408cd817f66c/vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/base.py#L245-L255)), which sets torch's default dtype

items.author: shyeh25
items.summary: Muse Spark NVFP4 checkpoints currently only run with EP equal to TP (TP4/EP4, TP8/EP8); is rejected. Expert tensor parallelism (every rank holds all 256 experts and 1/TP of each expert's intermediate dim) removes per-rank expert load imbalance.
items.body:
## Motivation

Muse Spark NVFP4 checkpoints currently only run with EP equal to TP (TP4/EP4, TP8/EP8); `--ep-size 1` is rejected. Expert tensor parallelism (every rank holds all 256 experts and 1/TP of each expert's intermediate dim) removes per-rank expert load imbalance.

Muse applies a post-expert RMSNorm to each (token, expert) row before the router-weighted top-k sum, so with expert TP each row has to be all-reduced before the norm, and the usual "sum, then all-reduce" MoE finalize does not apply. ## Motivation

The Muse Spark extend kernel `_muse_extend_kernel` is VALU-bound. On MI355X the softmax arithmetic sets the pace of each 128-key tile, not the MFMAs and not memory. A sizable part of the remaining VALU work in the hot loop was address math that is the same for every tile, or could be folded at compile time.

This PR removes that work. The kernel gets about 9% faster, and Muse Spark prefill TTFT drops by 1.5% to 7.1% at 32K to 256K prompt tokens.

items.body:
## Summary

The overlap scheduler prepares decode step N+1 while forward N runs, but with HiSparse the scheduler thread blocked every step on host syncs in the swap-in bookkeeping. The CPU therefore waited for the whole forward graph, then did ~2 ms of batch preparation, and only then launched forward N+1, leaving a 1.5-2.5 ms GPU idle gap per decode step on GLM-5.2 and DeepSeek-V4. This PR removes the remaining per-step host syncs so the scheduler overlaps with the GPU again. There is no kernel, policy or stream-ordering change.

items.title: [None][fix] Bound autotuner cache I/O on slow shared filesystems
items.author: ziyixiong-nv
items.summary: When points at a shared filesystem, every rank takes one exclusive lock to load the cache when an session starts, and takes it again to save at the end. Each save reads the whole JSON file, merges, and writes it back with an fsync.
items.body:
@coderabbitai summary

## Description

When `TLLM_AUTOTUNER_CACHE_PATH` points at a shared filesystem, every rank takes one exclusive lock to load the cache when an `autotune()` session starts, and takes it again to save at the end. Each save reads the whole JSON file, merges, and writes it back with an fsync. These calls run between collectives, so a stalled rank stalls all of them. During filesystem trouble, single saves took minutes, the ranks queued behind them, and the autotuner part of startup took close to an hour.

items.body:
Rank 0 creates the --save-hf directory and copies the non-weight files of --hf-checkpoint into it, then the
shard writers on other nodes open files in it. On NFS a client that looked the path up before rank 0 created it
can keep that negative lookup cached for a while, so a writer on another node fails to find a directory that
already exists on the server.

_SafetensorShardWriter now calls mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) on every rank that writes shards. The call
goes to the server and refreshes the cached entry; where the directory is already visible it does nothing.

items.body:
The SGLang patch stack adds TokenizerManager.post_process_weights, which always takes the writer side of
model_update_lock. During an in-place pause_generation the requests in flight keep the reader side, so the call
waits for requests that cannot finish while the engine is paused, and the weight update hangs. SGLang's own update
calls avoid this: update_weights_from_disk skips the writer lock while paused, and begin_weight_update and
end_weight_update go through _weight_update_session_call, which does the same. slime pauses the engines in place
whenever a weight update does not flush the cach

therefore asks Megatron to load optimizer state it has no template for. With Megatron 4b4acac9a the

items.title: Compute DSA split gradient norms from DTensor layouts in FullyShardedOptimizer
items.author: Autumn1998
items.summary: With MFSDP v2, DSA models fail at the first optimizer step. For models with a DSA indexer, the optimizer computes the indexer and non-indexer gradient norms on every step for logging.
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

With MFSDP v2, DSA models fail at the first optimizer step. For models with a DSA indexer, the optimizer computes the indexer and non-indexer gradient norms on every step for logging. The base `get_dsa_split_grad_norms` goes through `get_grad_norm_fp32`, which requires all DTensor gradients to share one mesh, but the non-indexer half mixes dense and expert gradients. `FullyShardedOptimizer` now computes both norms the way its `get_grad_norm` already does, from each gradient's own layout.

A DeepSeek-V4 Pro proxy on 64 GB200 with MFSDP v2 now runs past the first step.

items.title: [#22150][fix] Register RPC response futures before sending requests
items.author: itsrayeedscodespace
items.summary: A regular RPC reply can reach while is still awaiting the transport send. The response future is currently registered only after sending, so the reader discards that reply and the caller waits indefinitely with the default timeout.
items.body:
## Description

Fixes #22150.

A regular RPC reply can reach `_handle_regular_response` while `_call_async` is still awaiting the transport send. The response future is currently registered only after sending, so the reader discards that reply and the caller waits indefinitely with the default timeout. Remote errors can be lost in the same way.

Register the future under the existing admission/close lock before sending. Include the send in the existing `try/finally` so send failures and caller cancellation remove the registration. Fire-and-forget calls still send without allocating a response

`PPOTrainer._compute_old_log_prob` (v1) always sends `calculate_entropy=True` to `compute_log_prob`. items.title: [reward] fix: compare prime_code call-based outputs as plain builtins
items.author: Aarav500
items.summary: In, call-based tests compared the generated function's return value with. The generated code controls that object, so a subclass of or whose always returns got full reward on every call-based task.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8656. In `prime_code`, call-based tests compared the generated function's return value with `output == expected`. The generated code controls that object, so a subclass of `int` or `list` whose `__eq__` always returns `True` got full reward on every call-based task. Swapping the operands doesn't help, because Python tries a subclass's reflected `__eq__` first.

This adds `_to_builtin()` in `prime_code/testing_util.py` and applies it to the output right after the existing `json.dumps(output)` call. It rebuilds the value from plain `None`/`bool`/`int`/`float

With `use_fused_kernels=True` and `use_remove_padding=True`, the fused output layer (`FusedLinearForPPO`) projects **every** packed token onto the vocabulary, but the PPO path only ever reads the response positions. Kimi-K3.1 has 96 MLA attention heads. Neither fused DSA sparse-attention backend took that head count, so DSA fell back to the dense PyTorch reference, which materializes the `q @ k^T` score matrix (about 192 GiB per rank for a 64K sequence at CP=8) and runs out of memory. `slurmRunner` was assigned without `def` in `runLLMTestlistWithAgent`, making it a shared script Binding property across parallel stages. Declare the variable locally so each stage invocation keeps its own runner. This is a one-line fix; existing runtime-image propagation, timeout values and retry behavior are retained.

## Description

In decode, MegaMoE CuteDSL routed and computed the rows of CUDA graph padding requests and of attention-DP placeholder requests like real ones. Delta transfers reuse this group and device without changing the wire protocol

items.author: jagalindo
items.summary: Hypercorn wraps an bind in a socket object of its own and closes it when returns, and the server then closes the same descriptor again, which logs from every frontend at shutdown and could close an unrelated descriptor. This PR passes to hypercorn, so each own…

# What does this PR do?

Hypercorn wraps an `fd://` bind in a socket object of its own and closes it when `serve()` returns, and the server then closes the same descriptor again (`own_socket.close()`), which logs `OSError: [Errno 9] Bad file descriptor` from every frontend at shutdown and could close an unrelated descriptor. This PR passes `os.dup(own_socket.fileno())` to hypercorn, so each owner closes its own descriptor.

items.author: hxw12219
items.summary: Adds an opt-in FSDP engine option, (default ). RL losses read values only at response tokens, but the engine projects every packed token through the LM head.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Adds an opt-in FSDP engine option, `response_only_lm_head` (default `false`). RL losses read values only at response tokens, but the engine projects every packed token through the LM head. With the option on, the engine passes the packed rows that predict response tokens to the model as Transformers' `logits_to_keep`, so the eager and fused LM heads project only those rows. The values at response tokens are unchanged.

## Summary

Fixes #2519.

`_apply_model_patch` chained `git apply --verbose`, `git apply --verbose --reject` and `patch --batch --fuzz=5 -p1 -i` with `||` and no reset in between. ### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8504.

### What does this PR do?

Allow colocated NPU rollouts to explicitly select vLLM-Ascend's native IPC loading lifecycle. The trainer packs bounded byte buffers, exports a fresh IPC reference for each nonempty bucket, and waits for the worker to finish consuming that bucket. Leaving the option unset preserves the existing CUDA/ROCm, shared-memory and delta dispatch paths.

This is part 1 of a three-PR series: IPC, HCCL, then whole-stream reload.

items.title: [ray] fix: prevent master port races during worker startup
items.author: SeptPonts
items.summary: Prevent during Ray worker startup caused by the gap between selecting a master port and binding PyTorch's TCPStore. Previously, probed a free port with a temporary socket, closed it, and passed the port to workers.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Prevent `EADDRINUSE` during Ray worker startup caused by the gap between selecting a master port and binding PyTorch's TCPStore.

Previously, `RayWorkerGroup` probed a free port with a temporary socket, closed it, and passed the port to workers. Another process could claim that port before rank zero initialized its process group.

Rank zero now binds and retains the actual TCPStore before invoking the user worker constructor. It publishes the bound endpoint before that constructor can block waiting for peers, allowing the driver to start the remaining ranks.

items.title: Fix math_dapo Minerva extraction for markdown-decorated answers
items.author: siddhant-rajhans
items.summary: The existing regex captures the markers as part of the answer, so correct answers score -1.0. Fixes #8449 ## Root cause The Minerva answer pattern matches the literal "Answer" and captures everything after the colon to end of line.
items.body:
## Bug

Models commonly wrap the Minerva `Answer:` label in markdown bold/italic (`**Answer:** 42`, `Answer: **42**`, `**Answer:**\n\n42`). The existing regex captures the `*` markers as part of the answer, so correct answers score -1.0.

Fixes #8449

## Root cause

The Minerva answer pattern `(?i)Answer\s*:\s*([^\n]+)` matches the literal "Answer" and captures everything after the colon to end of line. When models decorate with markdown:

| Input | Extracted | After normalize | Score |
|---|---|---|---|
| `**Answer:** 42` | `** 42` | `**42` | -1.0 |
| `Answer: **42**` | `**42**` | `**42**` |

## Problem

For `k3` and `low_var_kl`, `compute_approx_kl` evaluates `exp(x) - 1 - x`, where `x = log_probs_base - log_probs`. This expression is nonnegative in real arithmetic, but subtracting 1 from a float32 exponential can erase the small KL term or make it negative when the policies are close.

items.author: 0z5a
items.summary: After that, the acceptance length is ~1.0 and rollout is slower than with speculative decoding off. How it happens: - slime's colocated sender calls with, and.
items.body:
## Problem

With `--sglang-speculative-algorithm DFLASH` and a colocated rollout engine, the first weight sync silently overwrites the DFLASH draft with target weights. After that, the acceptance length is ~1.0 and rollout is slower than with speculative decoding off.

- slime's colocated sender calls `update_weights_from_tensor` with `serialized_named_tensors`, `load_format="flattened_bucket"` and `weight_version`. It sets neither `selector` nor `disable_draft_model`.

items.title: fix(data): give uniform reward groups exactly zero advantage
items.author: saloni-garg
items.summary: When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about …
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In `_post_process_rewards` the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about an ulp instead of zero. With std normalization on, the residue is then divided by its own std, which turns it into a small nonzero advantage shared by the whole group.

Small reproduction on current main (a group of 16 rollouts that all scored 0.3, `grpo` with `grpo_std_normalization`):

-
discussion: The nonzero advantages for uniform fractional rewards reproduce on `main`. I ran the grouped-reward tests at `0063710` on CPU with PyTorch 2.13.0: uniform groups produce exact zeros, and the mixed-group and nonfinite-reward cases pass too.
Thank you for checking, and for reproducing it on main as well. Glad the tests hold up on your side too. Happy to run anything else you would like to see here.

## Summary

[FlashREINFORCE](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/labs-molt/pull/116) (NVIDIA molt) is critic-free RL with one rollout per prompt, built for asynchronous rollout. It is not a new loss but a combination of four pieces. slime already had two of them; this PR adds the other two.

| Piece | slime |

| Advantage: reward minus the mean reward of the whole rollout batch; no prompt groups, no std normalization, no whitening | **new**: `--advantage-estimator flash_reinforce` |

items.title: fix(sglang): validate deployment config before launch
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.
items.body:
## Background

Multi-model SGLang configuration was resolved incrementally while deployment side effects were already being prepared. Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.

## Problem

The config path did not validate whole-file invariants such as duplicate model names, multiple weight-updated models, complete engine topology, PP/TP consistency, or multi-node divisibility before launch.

## Solution

- Resolve every model and validate the complete config before placement or router startup.
- Reject unknown model fields

items.author: CharlesXu-HQ

## Background

`RayTrainGroup.create()` allocates training actors sequentially, discovers the rank-0 rendezvous address, initializes every actor, and optionally attaches the rollout manager.

## Problem

A failure at any of those stages left already-created actors alive. Rank 0 was especially vulnerable because it was added to `_actor_handlers` only after its rendezvous lookup succeeded. The non-empty handler list also prevented a clean retry.

## Solution

- Register each actor immediately after creation, before rank-0 rendezvous lookup.

items.title: fix(sglang): bound local server startup waits
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.
items.body:
## Background

Locally managed SGLang servers are polled through `/health_generate` before rollout initialization can continue.

## Problem

The startup poll had neither a request timeout nor an overall deadline. A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.

## Solution

- Add `--sglang-server-startup-timeout` with a positive finite value and a conservative 600-second default.
- Use a monotonic deadline and cap every health request by both five seconds and the remaining startup budget.
- Reject readiness

## Background

Slime resumes PPO training from actor, optional critic, and rollout-data checkpoints. Each model rank reports the next rollout ID after loading, while rollout data is restored from the preceding completed rollout.

The startup path previously selected one set of returned IDs without checking that:

- all actor ranks loaded the same rollout
- all critic ranks loaded the same rollout
- actor and critic checkpoints agree

items.title: fix(rollout): support fan-out results in group reward models
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: Those paths expect, so fan-out generation and group rewards could not be combined.
items.body:
## Background

A custom generation function may return multiple training segments for one input. `generate_and_rm_group` preserves that result as `list[list[Sample]]`.

## Problem

When `group_rm` is enabled, the nested result was passed directly to the group reward function and trace helper. Those paths expect `list[Sample]`, so fan-out generation and group rewards could not be combined.

## Solution

- Flatten one level before tracing and invoking the group reward function.
- Assign returned rewards to the same leaves in stable fan-out order.
- Preserve the original nested return shape for d

items.title: fix(rollout): handle nested aborted fully-async results
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: An aborted leaf inside a fan-out result could therefore enter the completed queue. Requeuing that nested output directly is also invalid because the next generation expects a flat input group.
items.body:
## Background

`generate_and_rm_group` supports custom generation that fans one input out into `list[Sample]`, so a fully-async task can return `list[list[Sample]]`.

## Problem

The done callback inspected only the outer list. An aborted leaf inside a fan-out result could therefore enter the completed queue. Requeuing that nested output directly is also invalid because the next generation expects a flat input group.

## Solution

- Snapshot the flat input group before generation can mutate it.
- Inspect one-level fan-out leaves for `Sample.Status.ABORTED`.
- Requeue the pristine flat snapshot

items.title: fix(rm_hub): stop substring-matching gpqa letter labels and short answers
items.author: shaurya416
items.summary: Fixes #2409 ## Problem falls back to a text match when no option letter can be extracted from the reply. That fallback (1) appended a one-letter gold label as answer text, and (2) searched each candidate as a raw substring of the normalized reply.
items.body:
Fixes #2409

## Problem

`compute_gpqa_reward` falls back to a text match when no option letter can be extracted from the reply. That fallback (1) appended a one-letter gold label as answer text, and (2) searched each candidate as a raw substring of the normalized reply. A reply that never answers, for example `I'm sorry, but I can't help with that.`, therefore scored 1.0 whenever the gold letter (`a`, `b`, `c`) occurred inside a word, and a short numeric choice such as `11` matched inside `2011` or `111`.

## Approach

- A one-character label that is a valid option letter is no longer added t

items.author: heyxingxing
items.summary: Fully-async generation, data-source and requeue failures currently only reach the logs. The consumer can wait forever for a full batch or silently skip already-consumed groups.
items.body:
Fully-async generation, data-source and requeue failures currently only reach the logs. The consumer can wait forever for a full batch or silently skip already-consumed groups. Preserve the first failure and raise it in the consumer with its original cause; stop scheduling work, cancel in-flight tasks, and prevent automatic replacement of the failed worker. Explicit ABORTED retries and intentional shutdown cancellation keep their existing behavior.

Closes https://github.com/THUDM/slime/issues/2399

## Problem

`MegatronTrainRayActor.init()` backs up the actor and then loads reference, teacher, or old-actor checkpoints into the same model.

Without `--offload-train`, initialization leaves the last auxiliary checkpoint active. Both training entry points synchronize rollout weights before the first training step, so distributed or disk-based synchronization can publish auxiliary weights instead of the resumed actor.

For one resumed run:

| | rollout logprob | reference logprob | actor logprob |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Before | -0.1106 | -0.1111 | -0.1471 |
| After | -0.1088 | -0.1421 | -0.1

## Summary

Fix CUDA autocast from downcasting the FP32 reduction used by VIME's fused PPO entropy path.

Under CUDA autocast, `torch.einsum` can run at a reduced precision even when both operands were explicitly promoted to FP32. The result is saved for entropy backward, so the precision loss affects both the reported entropy value and its gradient.

This change keeps only that CUDA reduction outside autocast and adds a one-GPU regression suite covering FP16/BF16 autocast, masked/unmasked log-prob paths, metric-only/gradient entropy, and chunked/non-chunked execution.

## Description

items.body:
## Problem

Training and evaluation launch rollout tasks concurrently at three levels: samples within a rollout group, rollout groups within a training batch, and samples within an evaluation batch.

When one task raises an exception, the exception is propagated but the unfinished sibling tasks are not cancelled. They can continue generation or reward computation after the rollout has failed, wasting resources and potentially leaving unobserved task exceptions in the event loop.

## Fix

At each concurrency boundary, cancel unfinished sibling tasks and wait for their cleanup before re-raising

items.body:
Enabling KL (--kl-coef 0.1 or --use-kl-loss) without --ref-load used to die in slime_validate_args with `TypeError: _path_exists: path should be string, bytes, os.PathLike or integer, not NoneType`, because it stat'd args.ref_load before checking it was set. The sibling OPD check just below already guards for None first.

This adds the same guard: ref_load unset now raises a ValueError telling the user to pass --ref-load, and a ref_load that points nowhere still raises the original FileNotFoundError. Two unit tests cover both cases.

## Summary

`_parse_extra_env_vars` split each assignment on every `=` and then kept only the second component. For example:

was parsed as:

In the agentic rollout path, each agent turn sends a request to SGLang through the SGLang router. When a request is cancelled or hits the client-side read timeout, Slime must explicitly abort the corresponding SGLang request to release its scheduler slot and KV-cache resources.

items.body:
## Problem

In non-colocated full NCCL weight updates with pipeline-parallel training and multiple independent SGLang rollout engines, each PP source creates a custom `slime-pp_<rank>` group containing itself and every engine GPU.

The PP sources are Ray actors invoked concurrently. Each rollout-engine actor uses a blocking HTTP call to join a group and processes methods serially. If engine 0 starts PP0 while engine 1 starts PP1, each group waits for the request queued behind the other engine's blocking call. The existing rollout-engine lock only covers later broadcasts, so it cannot prevent t

items.author: EazyReal
items.summary: OPD samples from the temperature-scaled student distribution, so leaving the teacher at its implicit default computes, not the matched-temperature objective. Passing the rollout temperature through sampling parameters is currently a no-op, while pinning it to …
items.body:
## Problem

Thanks to @kkyyxhll for catching in #2319 that SGLang ignores `sampling_params.temperature` when it computes input/prefill log-probs. OPD samples from the temperature-scaled student distribution `p_T`, so leaving the teacher at its implicit default computes `KL(p_T || q_1)`, not the matched-temperature objective `KL(p_T || q_T)`.

Passing the rollout temperature through sampling parameters is currently a no-op, while pinning it to `1.0` only makes the mismatched behavior explicit. Supporting the real-temperature case requires changing the SGLang input-logprob path.

## Summary

Fix IPv6 URL construction in the vLLM engine control plane.

## Problem

The vLLM subprocess requires an unbracketed IPv6 address when binding
the server, while an IPv6 literal must be enclosed in brackets when
used as the host component of an HTTP URL.

Previously, the health-check path could construct an invalid URL such
as:

`http://2001:db8::1:8000/health`

instead of:

`http://[2001:db8::1]:8000/health`

The health check may then keep retrying failed requests, making engine
startup appear to be stuck.
